parsed.strategic_reason: The grant funds statewide crash data system modernization and standardized electronic data transfer, which most closely aligns with G5.O1's focus on data infrastructure, integration, and data-driven decision-making.
parsed.strategic_evidence_quote: modernization of States’ crash data collection systems
parsed.eligibility_evidence_quote: State crash data owners and custodians for each of the 50 States, the District of Columbia; the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico; the United States Virgin Islands; Guam; American Samoa; the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands; and the Secretary of the Interior, acting on behalf of an Indian Tribe.
parsed.operational_reason: No NCDHHS division owns or operates the statewide crash data repository; that function sits with the state transportation/motor vehicle agency rather than health and human services.
restrictions: State match: recipients must contribute at least twenty (20) percent of State funds for eligible activity costs.
Data-transfer deadline: recipients must certify they will electronically transfer crash data to NHTSA beginning no later than five years from the effective date of award.
Coordination: if multiple state entities are responsible for the crash data repository, the State must appoint one point of contact for the application.
parsed.major_risk: NCDHHS is likely not the statewide crash data owner or custodian, so this opportunity probably belongs with NCDOT and would require interagency coordination plus a state match for a system outside DHHS authority.
parsed.one_line_rationale: Crash data system modernization aligns with operational data infrastructure, but NCDHHS does not own crash data; it likely belongs to NCDOT, so not recommended.
